summary: Dhammapala is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under K. L. Dhammajoti. He served as a visiting assistant professor there in 2013.

Dharmananda Kosambi was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University in 1926. He held posts at the University of Calcutta (~1906–1908), Harvard (~1910–1931), Gujarat University (~1920–1928), and Saint Petersburg State University (~1929–1931).
Dhirendra Mohan Datta was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held appointments at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).
Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar in the fields of philosophy and Indology who studied under David Friedman and traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He held positions at the Open University (attested 2017) and the University of Chester (2019).
Di Luo is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who completed a PhD at the University of Southern California (attested 2016) under the supervision of Sonya S. Lee.

Diana L. Eck is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Smith College, SOAS, and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. Around 1976, she began a long-standing professorship in comparative religion and Indian studies at Harvard.

Diana Lange is a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and history who studied at Leipzig, Tibet University, Humboldt University, and EPHE. She worked extensively at Humboldt University, the University of Hamburg, and became Professor of Central Asian History and Cultures at Humboldt in 2025.

Diane A. Lichtenstein completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1977. In 2005, she was attested as an adjunct professor of anthropology at Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane Elizabeth Riggs is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned her PhD at UCLA under William M. Bodiford. She held visiting posts at Pepperdine and Kenyon College, later joining Western Michigan University (attested 2017).
Diane L. Howard is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who conducted graduate studies at McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen (attested 1982).
Dickwela Piyananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the Catholic University of America under Siegfried A. Schulz (attested 1974).

Diego Loukota is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed an MA at Peking University and earned his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2019.

Dieter B. Kapp was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his doctorate at Heidelberg University under Hermann Berger. He taught at Heidelberg and served as director of the Institute for Indology and Tamil Studies at the University of Cologne (1990–2006).
Dieter George was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who served at the Prussian State Library from around 1972 to 1985.

Dieter Gunkel is a linguist and Indologist who studied at UCLA (~2004–2010). He held posts at the University of Munich (2010–2017), the University of Richmond (2017–2024), and the University of California, Los Angeles (2024).

Dieter Schlingloff is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Göttingen and Humboldt University under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held professorships at Kiel University (1968–1971), the University of Munich (1972–1996), and the University of Leipzig (2005).
Dieter Schrapel is an Indologist who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau (attested 1970).

Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD and completed his Habilitation at the University of Bonn, where he served as a professor from 1978 to 2007. He also founded and managed the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Dietmar Rothermund was a historian and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (1959). He spent his main career at Heidelberg University, holding the Chair of the History of South Asia from 1968 to 2001.
